Guides for what med ed won't teach you

Built from lived experience by a resident who has sat on both sides of the table. Priced for a student budget, readable on a phone between rotations.

MOST POPULAR GUIDE 01USMLE ACCOMMODATIONS

Testing Accommodations Workbook: MCAT, USMLE, COMLEX

Walk away with a complete accommodations request you can adapt to your own diagnosis. Inside: her full example application for USMLE Step 1, 2 and 3, a template for your personal statement, a template to hand your health professional for the supporting letter, the most requested DSM-5 criteria for ADHD, MDD, GAD, panic and PTSD, and workbook pages on how to disclose in applications and at school. Bonus: an anonymous personal statement from a medical student with ADHD, MDD and GAD.

$50.00 Grab the workbook POPULAR GUIDE 02ADVISING

Advising with Dr. Moss, 1 hr

Leave with a plan for your own situation, not general advice. One hour on failed exams, accommodations, a possible dismissal, a leave of absence, gap years, career pivots in or out of medicine, or applying with red flags or as an IMG.

Mock Interview with Dr. Moss

You get constructive feedback on your answers, body language, virtual background and overall presentation, and practice on the hard questions: academic failures, health conditions and disabilities, red flags, gap years and leaves of absence.

About Stephanie Moss, MD

SIDE A · THE PATIENT

The chart with her name on it

Her second year of medical school began with the reproduction block and ended with a diagnosis of endometriosis and infertility, after months of appointments and a laparoscopic surgery. She failed and retook two block exams, then took a leave of absence to focus on her health.

During that leave she failed Step 1 by a single point. After therapy, healing and months of study she retook it with accommodations, and fought her insurer for months to cover her egg stimulation and freezing.

SIDE B · THE DOCTOR

The coat with her name on it

Today she is a PGY-3 psychiatry chief resident for academics at Rosalind Franklin University, previously chief for medical student education and resident wellness, with a Medical Doctorate from Rush Medical College.

She co-founded the Chicago Homelessness and Health Response Group for Equity, gave her first talks on trauma-informed medicine with the Illinois Academy of Family Physicians, and turned the path she had to find alone into the map she never had.

“Humanizing medicine means seeing the person, not just the patient.” STEPHANIE MOSS, MD
